subject: Lavaan error: Initial model-implied matrix (sigma) is not positive definite

messages.author: 9bf6faee5a3b3ffe
messages.subject: Lavaan error: Initial model-implied matrix (sigma) is not positive definite
parts:
Hi there, 

When I create this model it works fine: 

model1 <- 'poorbond =~ HatedChild + PhysAbuseChild + LovedChild + SexAbuseChild
HatedChild~~LovedChild
HatedChild~~PhysAbuseChild
HatedChild~~SexAbuseChild
IQ_0~poorbond
IQ_0~~AgeAssessT0 + Sex
EducCompleteAge_0~~poorbond + IQ_0'

fit <- sem(model1, data=UKBio)
summary(fit, fit.measures=TRUE, standardized=TRUE)

However, when I add another variable 'PG_score' to the model below I get the error:  

  Error in lav_model_estimate(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavpartable = lavpartable,  : 
  lavaan ERROR: initial model-implied matrix (Sigma) is not positive definite;
  check your model and/or starting parameters.

model2 <- 'poorbond =~ HatedChild + PhysAbuseChild + LovedChild + SexAbuseChild
HatedChild~~LovedChild
HatedChild~~PhysAbuseChild
HatedChild~~SexAbuseChild
IQ_0~poorbond
IQ_0~PG_score
IQ_0~~AgeAssessT0 + Sex
EducCompleteAge_0~~poorbond + IQ_0'


I am not sure if this error is because of the way I am specifying the model. However, I have tried to input this variable a number of different ways and into a simple mediation model, and I still get the same error. This variable ranges from a score of -0.000276993 to 0.000282878. 


Any thoughts on this? Thanks in advance for your help!

messages.author: ad188126f9138663
messages.subject: Re: Lavaan error: Initial model-implied matrix (sigma) is not positive definite
parts:
Emma,
  In light of the very small range of PG_score, the first thing that you might consider is whether the covariance matrix in your data is ill-scaled.  Are all the variances in your sample scaled to differ by less than a ratio of 1:100?  if you are not already familiar with this idea, this is an important data screening step in any SEM analysis.  You can find the procedure for resolving this described in Rex Kline's textbook or any comparable book.  It basically involves multiplying variables by multiples of 10 to adjust the variances.

Keith
